To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

13CH3 probes are more sensitive than 13CHD probes in NMR experiments that exploit a TROSY-type effect, and that this is the main reason why 13CH3 labeling is the method of choice for NMR studies of supra-molecules.

(i) the sensitivity of 13C-13C correlation experiments in highly deuterated proteins and particles can be improved by 1.5–2 fold through selective methyl labeling with 13CH2D, (ii) the sensitivity of experiments that correlate 13C and 13C with 1H is improved by a similar factor through the use of 13CH2 and 13CH3 probes, (iii) the utility of 1H-detected 13C
the sensitivity of NMR experiments on supra-molecular systems with methyl groups is higher for samples labeled with 13CH 3 than for 13CHD 2 probes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and implementation of novel strategies and methods for the solution NMR characterization of supra-molecular assemblies.
the development of new strategies and methods for the study of large protein complexes, in particular the proteasome and its complexes.
the development of new NMR techniques and their application to the solution structure analysis of high molecular weight complexes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
13CHD labeling is a good compromise for most NMR experiments and that 13CH3 labeling should only be used when sensitivity is a limiting factor.

13CH3 labeling is the method of choice for NMR studies on high molecular weight particles, and that the use of 13CHD3 labeling is only required if the 1J13CHD3 coupling constant is to be exploited in structural studies.
both methods are complementary. 13CHD3 labeling is superior in terms of spectral dispersion and resolution, whereas 13CH3-labeling is superior in terms sensitivity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
13C- and 15N-labeled proteins with 13CH2 or 13CH3 groups on Leu, Ile, Val, Ala, and Thr sidechains are the optimal starting material for NMR studies of high molecular-weight complexes.
the use of 13CHD probes in combination with HMQC-TROSY experiments will provide the most efficient labeling strategy for the study of large protein complexes by NMR spectroscopy.
13CH3 labeling of Ile, Val, Leu residues is a highly effective method for studies of large supra-molecular assemblies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of 13CHD probes is a viable option for studies of large molecular complexes.
, in the case of supra-molecular complexes of 100 kDa and larger, the sensitivity of spectra of Ile, Val, Leu 13CH3 probes is comparable to the sensitivity of 13CH2 probes in 15N,13C-labeled samples.
13C- and 13CD2-labeled Ile, LeU, Val probes are both suitable for the study of high molecular weight proteins, with 13CH2D2 probes offering a significant sensitivity advantage over the 13CH3 probes.
